name: Plant cell
short_description: The companion umbrella subject to the animal cell: the generic textbook plant cell, rendered for contrast — a boxy cell shaped by its rigid cellulose wall, with the plasma membrane just inside, ONE huge watery central vacuole (tonoplast-bounded) pressing everything to the edges, green lens-shaped chloroplasts with coin-stack grana, a peripheral nucleus, smaller cristae-filled mitochondria, rough ER, a Golgi stack and plasmodesmata channels through the wall.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; boxy wall + membrane + dominant pale vacuole with tonoplast all correct on the first try, but four genuine defects on magnified crops: the dusty-purple heterochromatin is painted OUTSIDE the blue double envelope as a scalloped rind (the set's classic inverted-nucleus failure), the chloroplast interiors are continuous lengthwise stripes instead of separate coin-stack grana, several unexplained solid steel-blue blobs float in the strip, and one chloroplast is empty. Fix-prompt: separate coin-stack grana with stroma gaps, layered inside-the-envelope nucleus, mitochondria as the only blue-toned organelles)
textbook.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; grana now read as separate coin-stacks — fixed — but the heterochromatin rind sits OUTSIDE the envelope again, the mitochondria mutated into ribosome-dotted ER/mito hybrids clustered in an accordion, the blue blobs persist, and a literal letter-shaped 'V' glyph plus several caret marks are baked into the wall where plasmodesmata were requested. Fix: plasmodesmata dropped from the prompt, nucleus described as ordered concentric layers, mitochondrial membranes stated dot-free)
textbook.3: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; wall now clean with no glyphs and mitochondria smooth-skinned with wavy rose cristae, chloroplasts each carrying 3 stacked-disc grana — but the magnified crop shows the purple heterochromatin wreath STILL outside the blue envelope ring, the third occurrence of the same countable failure. Escalated to gemini-3-pro-image per the 2-failure rule, one attempt late)
textbook.4: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; ACCEPTED as the textbook final and primary labelled figure. Verified on magnified crops of all four quadrants: no letters, numbers or callouts anywhere — notable because the pro tier baked full printed labels into the sibling animal-cell plate. MEASURED on the image: boxy rounded-rectangle outline set by a thick layered sand wall; ONE thin teal plasma membrane line hugging the wall's inner face (teal confirmed by pixel sample at (400,163)); ONE kidney-shaped pale-blue central vacuole with its own darker tonoplast line — its sectional area is only ≈ half of the cell, short of the >3/4 the prompt asked for (recorded as compromise); nucleus pressed to the upper-right periphery with heterochromatin clumps correctly INSIDE the double envelope, amber pores, one terracotta nucleolus with no boundary line; 6 chloroplasts counted, each holding 3-7 separate coin-stack grana with stroma gaps; 4 clearly smaller rose mitochondria with wavy cristae, none dotted; ribosome-dotted rough-ER arcs around the nucleus; ONE dull grey-sage Golgi fan; ribosome dot scatter and fine thread strokes. Compromise: no plasmodesmata (deliberately removed from the prompt after they induced letter-like glyphs in attempt 2), so that label is omitted from the SVG)

sem.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; convincing boxy fractured-wall composition with neighbour stubs and a dominant smooth vacuole dome, but two drawn-on defects at 2x zoom: every coral mitochondrion carries a literal dark zigzag scribble ON its intact surface (reads as a handwriting-like 'wwww' mark, not fractured cristae), and the chloroplast interiors are rectangular machine-grille insets with ruler-straight blinds. Fix-prompt: fractured-open organelles with three-dimensional relief only, no drawn lines on any surface)
sem.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; ACCEPTED as the sem final. Verified on magnified crops (top fracture, right chloroplast column, bottom mitochondria row, nucleus corner): no letters, numbers or scale bars anywhere. MEASURED: boxy cell with a thick granular fractured sand wall seated among neighbouring cells' wall stubs at the frame edges (appropriate for a wall-bound tissue); a thin smooth membrane lining inside the wall rim; the interior dominated by one vast smooth pale blue-grey vacuole dome (≈ half the interior in section — shown as the intact tonoplast surface rather than an opened cavity, an honest SEM-fracture reading, recorded); 6 green lens chloroplasts lodged along the wall, the broken ones showing organic parallel thylakoid lamellae in real relief — separate coin-stack grana are NOT resolved, the membranes read as one lamellae array per chloroplast (recorded as compromise; grana are carried by the other three styles); 5 clearly smaller coral mitochondria whose broken faces show wavy parallel cristae shelves with real depth (the drawn-on zigzags are gone); one granular dusty-violet nucleus sphere pressed into a corner with pale ER sheets around it. A few thin thread strands bridge the fracture at top — read as fibrous strands, acceptable at SEM realism)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; good wall, membrane and organelle materials, but the central vacuole renders as a shallow swimming-pool filling only the bottom third instead of dominating the interior, one large green chloroplast lies ON/INSIDE the vacuole pool (organelles must stay in the peripheral strip), the ER is drawn as thick dark charcoal slugs, and white fibre tufts sprout from the wall. Fix-prompt: vacuole rising floor-to-top as one vast clear glassy mass with every organelle in the thin layer between it and the wall; smooth clay-like wall; pale translucent ER)
3d.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; ACCEPTED as the 3d final and labelled. Verified on magnified crops of all four quadrants plus nucleus/ER close-ups: no letters or numbers anywhere. MEASURED: boxy cutaway block with thick matte sand wall (cut faces showing its clay-like thickness), ONE glossy teal plasma membrane lining it; ONE huge glassy faintly-blue vacuole ball rising through the interior, perfectly empty, with a soft specular tonoplast surface (pixel-verified rim at (640,314)) — in section it reads as ≈ 40-50% of the interior rather than the >3/4 asked for (recorded); nucleus pressed to the left wall with TWO concentric translucent blue envelope shells, crisp amber porthole pores, purple chromatin berries INSIDE against the rim and one terracotta nucleolus with no shell; 6 translucent green chloroplast capsules along the strip, each with an internal accordion of stacked green thylakoid discs (grana as one accordion per chloroplast rather than several separate stacks — minor, recorded); 4 clearly smaller cut mitochondria with steel-blue rims and wavy dusty-rose cristae; beaded translucent rough-ER ribbons flowing out of the nucleus; ONE dull sage Golgi pancake stack; black ribosome specks throughout. Minor artefacts accepted and recorded: a faint horizontal seam line across the vacuole ball, a few stray white fibre wisps on the outer wall, and no visible plasmodesmata)

watercolor.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; full-bleed aged paper, boxy walled cell, calm dominant vacuole and lovely coin-disc chloroplasts — but faint lavender debris blobs float INSIDE the vacuole sap, the nucleus chromatin+pores render as tidy decorative capsules, and no Golgi stack exists anywhere on the plate)
watercolor.2: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the vacuole is now calm and empty and every chloroplast carries two beautifully striated coin-stack grana, but the nucleus interior is painted as a literal FLOWER — a regular purple petal rosette around the nucleolus, decorative rather than chromatin — and the Golgi is again absent. Fix-prompt: irregular ragged chromatin mottle, prominent grey-sage Golgi pile)
watercolor.3: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the Golgi appeared and the chromatin became a cog-like ring — closer but still geometric — while a NEW defect arrived: the vacuole opens toward the nucleus in a neck and a spray of purple speckles drifts INSIDE the sap. Third genuine flash failure -> escalated to gemini-3-pro-image)
watercolor.4: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; ACCEPTED as the watercolor final, labelled black-on-paper. Verified on magnified crops of all four quadrants: no letters or numbers anywhere; the warm cream paper reaches all four edges and corners with a soft grey wash halo painted directly on the paper (house convention). MEASURED: boxy ochre double-lined wall with anticlinal junction seams, teal membrane band pixel-verified at (470,193); ONE closed kidney-shaped vacuole in the palest watery blue, calm and perfectly empty, tonoplast ink line pixel-verified at (808,550) — ≈ 45-50% of the cell in section (short of >3/4, recorded); nucleus at the left periphery with an IRREGULAR mottled purple chromatin texture inside the double envelope (the flower/cog geometry finally gone) and one soft terracotta nucleolus; 5 chloroplasts counted, each holding 4-7 separate striated coin-stack grana; 3 clearly smaller mauve-rimmed mitochondria with wavy rose cristae; dotted rough-ER arc bands around the nucleus; ONE prominent grey-sage Golgi pile; ribosome ink dots. The wall junction seams could be misread as plasmodesmata pit-fields but are not labelled)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons "Plagiomnium affine laminazellen.jpeg", CC BY-SA 3.0, Kristian Peters (Fabelfroh) - a genuine brightfield light micrograph of living moss (Plagiomnium affine) leaf cells, viewed directly: crisp polygonal cell-wall boundaries and each cell packed with dozens of distinct lens-shaped green chloroplasts - the subject's two defining features, individually readable. Honest caveats, all recorded: a GROUP of cells, not an isolated specimen (the true condition of a wall-bound tissue, and features stay readable, which is the skill's acceptance bar); a surface view of a whole mount, so vacuole, tonoplast, nucleus, mitochondria and ER are not resolvable in this modality - the illustrated styles carry those; the cells are moss lamina, not flowering-plant parenchyma. The plate has no text, scale bar or border, so per the rules NO AI cleaning was run; processing is fetch_reference.py's deterministic centre-crop of the 800x600 original to 600x600 and a stated 1.8x LANCZOS upscale to 1080x1080. Two alternatives rejected after viewing/checking: Cloroplasti Elodea.jpg (eyepiece photo, huge black vignette) and Onion Cells.jpg (epidermis - no chloroplasts)
decision: use gen-04 (gemini-3-pro-image) as final and primary labelled figure. Flash failed the same countable feature three times running - heterochromatin outside the nuclear envelope - plus a baked 'V' glyph in attempt 2; pro fixed the nucleus, kept clean unlettered surfaces, and drew 6 chloroplasts with separate coin-stack grana. Accepted compromises: vacuole ≈ half the section rather than >3/4; plasmodesmata deliberately omitted (they induced letter-like glyphs)

use gen-02 (gemini-2.5-flash-image) as final; attempt 1 drew literal zigzag scribbles on intact mitochondria and machine-grille chloroplast insets; the re-prompt (fractured organelles, relief-only surfaces) fixed both. Not labelled (SEM is the surface/fracture comparison plate, per set convention). Compromises: vacuole shown as intact dome, grana not resolved into separate stacks, thread strands at the fracture

use gen-02 (gemini-2.5-flash-image) as final; labelled figure built. Attempt 1 put the vacuole as a bottom pool with a chloroplast inside it; the floor-to-top clear-mass re-prompt fixed containment and dominance in one pass. Compromises: vacuole ≈ 40-50% of section, one accordion granum per chloroplast, faint seam on the vacuole ball, stray wall wisps

use gen-04 (gemini-3-pro-image) as final, labelled black-on-paper. Flash three times in a row put something wrong in or around the nucleus/vacuole (debris in the sap, a literal flower rosette as chromatin, a speckle spray through a vacuole neck); pro delivered irregular chromatin, a closed calm vacuole, 5 coin-stack chloroplasts and the Golgi in one pass
